title: Voz pasiva: circulación de ideas ilustradas

sections.content: Passive voice fits the spread of ideas naturally: ideas were disseminated, events were followed closely, an example was admired or feared — the reader's attention stays on the idea or event, not on naming every single person who read or reacted to it. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Nuevas ideas sobre la libertad y la igualdad fueron difundidas por el mundo atlántico mediante libros y periódicos.
items.english: New ideas about liberty and equality were spread across the Atlantic world through books and newspapers.

items.spanish: La independencia de Estados Unidos y la Revolución Francesa fueron seguidas de cerca por lectores criollos educados.
items.english: The independence of the United States and the French Revolution were followed closely by educated criollo readers.

items.spanish: Ese ejemplo fue admirado por algunos, pero también fue temido profundamente por muchos criollos propietarios de esclavos.
items.english: That example was admired by some, but was also deeply feared by many criollo slave-owners.

items.spanish: El ejemplo haitiano fue observado con gran atención por las élites criollas de todo el continente.
items.english: The Haitian example was watched with great attention by criollo elites across the continent.

sections.content: Fue admirado... pero también fue temido shows how two passive clauses with the same grammatical shape can hold a contradiction in balance — the same event, admired by some and feared by others, without needing separate sentences for each reaction.
